title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
kicker: Inside the three software suites protecting, governing, and migrating the world's most sensitive collaborative data.

epigraph.quote: Data without governance is a toxic liability waiting for a breach; data without resilience is a disaster waiting for a ransomware note. We provide the operational guardrails that allow enterprises to collaborate freely without terrorizing their Chief Information Security Officer.
epigraph.author: Dr. Tianyi (TJ) Jiang, CEO, AvePoint

web_blocks.html: Modern cloud collaboration comes with a hidden risk. When firms deploy Microsoft 365 or Salesforce, executives assume data is fully protected. In reality, cloud providers follow a Shared Responsibility Model. Microsoft ensures that servers, power, and networks stay online. But customers remain responsible for their data. That includes protection against deletions, ransomware, insider threats, and access permission sprawl.

AvePoint bridges this gap with its Confidence Platform. The software runs on Microsoft Azure across 14 sovereign data centers. It offers three core product suites. The Resilience Suite handles automated backup and disaster recovery. The Control Suite manages workspace lifecycle and records compliance. The Modernization Suite handles data migration and tenant consolidation. In addition, AvePoint Opus cleans data to prepare it for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

web_blocks.html: AvePoint serves three distinct customer tiers. Enterprise clients with over 5,000 seats account for 52% of total ARR. They buy through a direct sales team. Mid-market firms with 500 to 5,000 seats generate 28% of ARR. Small businesses with under 500 seats produce 20% of ARR. That SMB segment is AvePoint's fastest-growing channel. It is sold through more than 6,000 Managed Service Providers on cloud distribution marketplaces.

web_blocks.title: Concrete Customer Examples: How the Software Operates in Practice

web_blocks.html: Case Study 1: Resilience Suite at Mears Group. Mears Group manages 450,000 homes in the UK with 5,000 staff. They store tenant leases and repair logs in Microsoft 365. Native Microsoft recycle bins purge deleted files after 30 to 90 days. If an admin deletes a shared mailbox, data can be lost permanently. Mears deployed AvePoint Cloud Backup. The software runs four automated backups daily into encrypted Azure storage. When a shared mailbox was accidentally deleted, an administrator restored it in 90 seconds. Mears pays about $3 per user monthly. This provides inexpensive insurance against major regulatory fines.

Case Study 2: Control Suite at New Zealand Government. A New Zealand public ministry manages 131 terabytes of data in Microsoft 365. Remote work led to team sprawl. Over 14,000 external guest accounts accumulated over four years. Working with Datacom, the agency deployed AvePoint Cloud Governance and Opus. Cloud Governance automated team creation with approval rules and six-month timers. Opus scanned data and revoked access for 11,000 inactive guest users. That cut 80% of external attack risk in one weekend. It also purged 5,000 expired public records safely.

Case Study 3: Modernization Suite at Wellington Healthcare. A regional healthcare group in New Zealand consolidated clinics into one cloud tenant. They had to migrate 2.3 terabytes of clinical records without downtime. New Zealand law requires ten years of record retention. The group used AvePoint Fly Migration. Fly mapped legacy permissions to target Entra ID groups. It ran delta syncs over weekends. It set rollback points before each transfer batch. The team onboarded 50 clinicians in hours rather than three weeks. Patient care continued without interruption.

Case Study 2: The Control Suite (Cloud Governance & Opus) in National Government Administration. Consider a sovereign New Zealand Government public service ministry overseeing national policy, welfare distribution, and statutory records across more than 131 terabytes of collaborative Microsoft 365 data. Following the shift to remote work, the ministry experienced severe collaborative sprawl: employees had spun up thousands of unmonitored Microsoft Teams channels, department document libraries were cluttered with redundant files, and over 14,000 external guest accounts had accumulated over four years, granting former consultants and third-party vendors lingering access to confidential Cabinet policy drafts.

Data volumes continue to expand at an exponential pace. Enterprise teams create thousands of documents and chats every week. Without automated tools, IT teams cannot track access rights. Sensitive records end up exposed to unauthorized users. AvePoint solves this problem with continuous background scanning.

The platform also supports hybrid cloud deployments. Many defense and banking clients keep some servers on-premises. AvePoint manages both cloud and local environments from one dashboard. This hybrid capability expands its addressable market across sovereign government agencies.

book_paragraphs: To understand what AvePoint actually does for a living, you and I need to strip away the software industry jargon and look at what happens inside an enterprise IT department on a Monday morning. Imagine you are the Chief Information Officer of a global financial services firm with twenty thousand employees. Two years ago, your board of directors approved a massive digital transformation budget to move everyone to Microsoft 365. Your employees love it. They collaborate on Teams, share financial models on OneDrive, and co-author strategic memos on SharePoint.

Then, one morning, your Chief Information Security Officer walks into your office with a white face. A junior compliance officer has accidentally shared a SharePoint folder containing executive compensation plans and unannounced acquisition targets with a link set to 'Anyone with this link inside the organization.' For twenty-four hours, that link was active. Even worse, your IT audit team discovers that over the past three years, your employees have created six thousand separate Microsoft Teams channels—half of which were for temporary lunch clubs or defunct projects—and more than eight thousand external consultants, former vendors, and temporary interns still possess active guest credentials granting them access to internal files.

You call Microsoft support. They give you the cold reality of the Shared Responsibility Model. Microsoft provides the highway, but you own the car and everything inside it. Microsoft's native recycle bins hold deleted files for thirty or ninety days. . But they do not provide automated cross-department lifecycle governance, they do not automatically revoke orphaned guest credentials. They do not provide granular, item-level disaster recovery across multiple clouds. If you suffer a coordinated ransomware attack that encrypts your SharePoint document libraries, Microsoft cannot simply roll your tenant back to 9:15 AM without destroying every other email and message sent by your twenty thousand employees all morning.

This is where AvePoint enters the picture. AvePoint does not replace Microsoft; it acts as the essential trust, governance, and safety harness wrapped around Microsoft's cloud infrastructure. Think of Microsoft 365 as an extraordinarily powerful, high-speed locomotive. AvePoint provides the automated braking systems, the signal switches, the emergency escape hatches, and the digital manifests that ensure the train stays on the tracks.

Let us walk through the three core suites that generate AvePoint's revenue. First is the Resilience Suite, anchored by AvePoint Cloud Backup. In the old days of on-premises computing, backing up a server was simple: you plugged a tape drive into a rack and ran a script at midnight. In a multi-tenant cloud environment where data is scattered across Exchange mailboxes, Teams chats, Planner boards, and Entra ID identity graphs, backup is an immensely complex engineering challenge. AvePoint captures four automated snapshots of an enterprise's entire cloud estate every single day, encrypts the data, and stores it in isolated Azure Blob storage. If an employee deletes an entire customer folder, or if an attacker encrypts a department drive, an administrator can search, locate, and restore that specific file in ninety seconds with zero downtime.

Second is the Control Suite, led by AvePoint Cloud Governance. This is the operational brain that prevents collaborative chaos. Instead of letting employees spin up hundreds of ungoverned Teams channels, Cloud Governance provides an intelligent self-service portal. An employee requests a team, selects whether it is internal or external. AvePoint automatically assigns access permissions, applies regulatory data loss prevention tags, and sets an automated expiration timer. Every quarter, the system sends an automated email to the team owner asking: 'Is this project still active? Do these external contractors still need access?' If the owner does not recertify, the workspace is automatically archived and deleted. It turns what would be thousands of hours of manual IT drudgery into background software automation.

Third is the Modernization Suite, powered by AvePoint Fly. Whenever two healthcare networks merge, or a bank acquires an insurance broker, corporate IT faces the nightmare of tenant consolidation. How do you move fifty terabytes of highly confidential patient data or client portfolios from three different cloud systems into one unified environment without corrupting file links or losing historical audit trails? Fly orchestrates the entire data pipeline, mapping user permissions, scheduling weekend delta syncs, and verifying data integrity with automated rollback checkpoints.

And now, consider the newest frontier: AvePoint Opus and artificial intelligence trust. Every Fortune 500 board is demanding that their enterprise deploy generative AI tools like Microsoft 365 Copilot. But here is the dirty secret of enterprise AI: Copilot is only as safe as your underlying data permissions. If a confidential board memo about impending layoffs is stored in an unclassified folder, any employee who prompts Copilot with 'What changes are planned for my department?' will see that confidential document summarized on their screen. AvePoint Opus acts as the digital sanitation crew. It scans petabytes of corporate data, identifies redundant, obsolete, and trivial files, flags overshared sensitive records, and cleans up access permissions before the AI engine is switched on. In the age of artificial intelligence, clean data governance is not an optional luxury; it is the non-negotiable prerequisite for enterprise survival.

Think about the legal liabilities that large multinational corporations face under modern regulatory frameworks like the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) or the Network and Information Security Directive (NIS2). Under GDPR Article 32, an organization that fails to maintain verifiable, tested backup and recovery procedures for citizen data faces statutory administrative fines of up to twenty million euros or four percent of global annual turnover. When you view AvePoint's subscription fee through that regulatory lens, the software is not a discretionary IT expense; it is statutory compliance insurance.

Notice how AvePoint designs its user interfaces to bridge the gap between technical system administrators and non-technical business managers. In traditional IT environments, granting or revoking access required writing custom PowerShell scripts or opening helpdesk tickets that sat in IT queues for three weeks. AvePoint built intuitive, web-based self-service dashboards where department managers can recertify project memberships with a single tap on their smartphone. By decentralizing governance to the business owners who actually know who should have access to what, AvePoint eliminates IT bottlenecks while dramatically strengthening security posture.

Consider also the profound operational leverage that comes from platform standardization across customer verticals. Whether AvePoint is deploying its Confidence Platform inside a sovereign defense ministry, a multinational pharmaceutical conglomerate, or a regional school district, the underlying core software engine remains identical. The same multi-tenant Azure architecture that enforces records retention in New Zealand also protects tenant data for housing authorities in the United Kingdom.

That architectural consistency means that every dollar invested in research and development benefits the entire customer estate simultaneously. Unlike bespoke IT consulting firms that must reinvent custom solutions for every new client engagement, AvePoint's Software-as-a-Service model captures pure software operating margins. This allows incremental revenue to drop straight down to the bottom line.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why the Shared Responsibility Model Is a Permanent Moat
book_callouts.text: Every novice technology investor asks the same question: 'Why doesn't Microsoft just build this themselves and kill AvePoint?' The answer lies in the fundamental economics of cloud hyperscalers. Microsoft's business model is selling Azure compute cycles, enterprise E5 seat licenses, and Copilot subscriptions. Microsoft does not want to become a bespoke, high-touch data governance and backup administrator for 400 million users with varying regulatory requirements across eighty sovereign jurisdictions. By establishing the Shared Responsibility Model as an industry standard, Microsoft actively encourages trusted partners like AvePoint to build the specialized governance layer, creating an enduring, high-margin niche that hyperscalers have zero incentive to commoditize.
